scenes.title: Astronauts aren't weightless
scenes.say: Astronauts on the space station aren't weightless. Gravity up there is still about *ninety percent* of what you feel right now.
scenes.source: NASA: the ISS orbits about 400 km up, where gravity is about 90% of surface strength

scenes.title: So why do they float?
scenes.say: So why do they float? Stay close, student. *Lumen,* take us up.

scenes.title: Welcome to orbit
scenes.say: Four hundred kilometers up. The station moves about {7.7|seven point seven} kilometers every *second.* One lap around Earth every ninety minutes.

scenes.title: Newton's cannonball
scenes.say: Newton imagined a cannon on a mountain. Fire slowly, the ball falls nearby. Fire faster, it lands farther away. Fire fast *enough,* and the ground curves away as fast as the ball falls.
scenes.source: Isaac Newton, A Treatise of the System of the World (1728). Simulated with real inverse-square gravity

scenes.title: Orbit = falling forever
scenes.say: That's an orbit. The station *is* falling. It just keeps missing the Earth. Everyone inside falls together, so they float.

scenes.title: The whole sky is falling

items: Falls toward Earth every second and keeps missing
Falls around the Sun, one lap per year

scenes.say: The Moon does the same thing. So does Earth around the Sun. The whole sky is *falling,* and missing.

scenes.say: Class dismissed. Go build something. Stop waiting for that *interview.*
